headline: Housing committee hears more testimony on condo rezoning lists

meeting.body: Maui County Council Housing and Land Use Committee
meeting.summary: The Housing and Land Use Committee heard more testimony on Resolutions 26-129 and 26-130 and plans to reconvene Thursday.
meeting.recap: Members took up Resolutions 26-129 and 26-130 together.[[0:03:16]] The meeting picked up public testimony where it had stopped at the last session.[[0:03:27]] A testifier opposed the proposal and said hotel zoning, called H3 and H4, is being taken advantage of.[[0:27:41]] A vacation rental association representative said 162 of the affected condo units sold from December 1 through August 14.[[0:45:00]] She said only 12 of those, or 7.4%, are confirmed as owner-occupied.[[0:45:00]] A testifier from a housing group opposed both resolutions.[[1:20:25]] She said fire survivors in temporary housing in Kīhei fear they must leave by August 31.[[1:27:05]] Another testifier said 11 similar properties fully inside the sea level rise area are not on the list.[[1:32:57]] The committee plans to reconvene Thursday at 9 a.m.[[2:39:07]]
decided: The chair recessed the meeting to reconvene Thursday at 9 a.m. on the same Teams link, with no vote taken.
meeting.next: The in-person meeting will be in the Council Chambers at the Kalana O Maui Building, 8th floor, 200 South High Street, Wailuku. The chair said testimony will likely continue at the start of the next session, with discussion later that day.

moments.q: Owner asks to be added to the list

trackerIssues.title: Ending apartment vacation rentals and hotel rezoning of 48 properties

issues.oneLine: A testifier described conditions for fire survivors living in temporary housing in Kīhei.
issues.why: The testifier said a focus group of fire survivor renters found more people are rent burdened than in the past.
issues.brief: The testifier said the temporary units are hotel rooms without kitchens.[[#1]] She said many residents there fear they must be out by August 31.[[#2]]
